description: Document Content Injection Attack Attackers could craft documents containing malicious content that might be interpreted or executed during document processing. This could include JavaScript in PDFs, macro-enabled Office documents, or specially crafted text content designed to exploit vulnerabilities in processing libraries. An attacker uploads a PDF containing JavaScript that exploits a vulnerability in the document processing pipeline, potentially gaining execution access to the Lambda environment or poisoning the Kendra index with malicious content.
references: recommendation: Implement comprehensive document content validation and sanitization
recommendation: Enhance Lambda execution environment security

description: Unauthorized Document Access via Kendra Search If Kendra index access controls are not properly configured or maintained, users could potentially search and retrieve content from documents they don't have permission to access. A regular user performs a search that returns sensitive information from documents belonging to other users or departments, bypassing intended access restrictions.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement robust ACL management in Kendra

description: Exposure of PII in Search Index Documents containing PII are processed and indexed without proper PII detection and redaction, making sensitive personal information searchable and potentially exposable through the search interface. A user searches for common patterns like email addresses or social security numbers, potentially retrieving PII from documents across the system.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement PII detection and redaction

description: Pre-signed URL Abuse If pre-signed URLs are generated with long expiration times or without proper restrictions, they could be shared or reused beyond their intended use, bypassing authentication and authorization controls. An authenticated user obtains a pre-signed URL and shares it with unauthorized users who can then upload documents to the system without proper authentication.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement strict pre-signed URL controls
recommendation: Enhance upload monitoring and control

description: Insecure Communication with Kendra Without proper TLS configuration and certificate validation, communications between system components and Kendra could be intercepted or tampered with. An attacker with network access could potentially intercept or modify data being sent to or from the Kendra index during document processing.

S3 Bucket Misconfiguration Improper S3 bucket configuration could allow unauthorized access to documents through public access settings, overly permissive bucket policies, or misconfigured ACLs. An attacker discovers a misconfigured bucket policy that allows listing or downloading of documents without proper authentication.
